evidence: app/src/routes/index.ts:35 — one undocumented internal contract (gracile-static hostname) guards every data route
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:104 — same sentinel in the [param] route
app/src/routes/index.client.ts:16-38 — client interactivity is vanilla DOM, avoiding Gracile's experimental CSR/hydration add-ons
app/package.json:6-9 — gracile 0.11.0 (latest stable), lit/vite within engine's declared peer ranges
reach.rationale: The app deliberately avoids every genuinely experimental Gracile surface (client router, premises, hydration) and uses only the documented stable core; the sole non-contract reliance is the internal 'gracile-static' build-time sentinel, used in central places.

evidence: app/src/routes/index.ts:35 — sentinel string duplicated inline rather than wrapped in a lib helper
app/src/routes/types/[name].ts:24, moves/[name].ts:28, abilities/[name].ts:19 — same check copy-pasted in each route
app/src/routes/types/index.ts:10 — guard missing entirely, so this handler fetches the API at build time
containment.rationale: Documented framework APIs live in the conventional places (document, routes, server.js), but the one unstable internal sentinel is spread verbatim across five route files and inconsistently applied — easy to swap in one module, but not isolated.

evidence: app/src/routes/index.ts:35-49 — stub return prevents a build-time API fetch, required by the spec ('don't fetch API data at build time')
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:110 — responseInit.status = 404 buys the encouraged HTTP 404 via the public typed API
app/server.js:5,10-11 — nodeAdapter/getClientBuildPath mirror the documented Express deployment verbatim
justification.rationale: The sentinel buys spec compliance no stable API provides (Gracile invokes handlers at build even in server mode, and the 404-status and Express-adapter uses are the documented idioms); no use is novelty-driven, only the imperfect consistency of the guard keeps it from full marks.

findings.issue: Handlers rely on the undocumented internal 'gracile-static' hostname sentinel (also app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:104, abilities/[name].ts:19, types/[name].ts:24, moves/[name].ts:28) to detect Gracile's build-time handler invocation; it matches 0.11.0 internals but appears nowhere in the docs and could change in a minor release.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single helper, e.g. lib/build-time.ts exporting isBuildTimeRender(url: URL), with a comment citing packages/engine/src/routes/render.ts, and add a Gracile version bump to the upgrade checklist.

findings.issue: This handler lacks the build-time guard the other five handlers have, so Gracile's build phase triggers a live API fetch here; harmless for the server output today (build-time props are discarded) but inconsistent and a real build-time data dependency if output ever flips to 'static'.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same early-return stub (or the shared helper) used in routes/index.ts:35.

findings.issue: Template reads props via `context.props.GET as any` (also in all other routes), discarding the type inference defineRoute provides for the handler→template contract.
findings.suggestion: Drop the `as any` casts and let defineRoute's types flow from the GET handler's return type; if the union with the build-time stub shape is awkward, narrow it in one shared type.

summary: This is a conservative app on a young framework: it uses only Gracile 0.11.0's documented stable core (defineRoute handler/document/template, node adapter, server output) plus long-stable Lit and peer-approved Vite 8, and pointedly avoids the framework's actual experimental features (client router, premises, hydration) in favor of vanilla DOM client scripts. The single unstable reliance is the undocumented 'gracile-static' build-time hostname sentinel, justified as the only way to honor the no-build-time-fetch requirement, but duplicated across five routes instead of wrapped. Overall risk is low and concentrated in one easily-isolated pattern.

experimentalApis.source: Undocumented internal contract; confirmed in packages/engine/src/routes/render.ts of gracile-web/gracile at the 0.11.0 release commit and current main (new URL(path, 'http://gracile-static') when invoking handlers at build time); absent from gracile.js.org docs and llms.txt
